answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate and 14-day expiration create a hard constraint. memory_c2 demonstrates the low-cost vendor has delivered reliable onboarding and accurate invoicing in the past, meeting the cost target independently. However, the 94% assembly line utilization creates material delivery risk if transition stumbles. A standard experiment approach (phased volume increase rather than full cutover) hedges this: it captures the cost win immediately while preserving the incumbent as a safety valve for the next 60–90 days. This avoids both the renewal cost of memory_c6 scenarios and the demand-side vulnerability of running sole-source at maximum utilization. The flag reflects that quality/delivery disruption could cascade into margin loss exceeding the savings; the decision preserves uncertainty by building in a validation checkpoint before full commitment.
